text:
alex: Heads-up — security scan + our threat intel flagged CVE-2026-0487 in `payload-parser` (npm). RCE via crafted header; PoC circulating on GH. Affects hosted API public ingress and Dedicated nodes that expose proxy. Need prioritization: emergency hotfix rollout or schedule in next maintenance window? Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2046

security-bot: scan-summary: severity=high; exploitability=public-poC; affected_hosts=hosted-api,dedicated-proxy; earliest_detection=1711999000; recommended_action=patch+rebuild

maya: :eyes: If PoC is public I lean emergency. Impact depends on whether customers use the vulnerable surface. Do we know which customer tiers are affected (esp enterprise/private)?

alex: Quick check — dedicated customers behind private networking largely unaffected unless they route traffic through public proxies. Hosted self-serve and some SMB customers definitely exposed. Priya has list of hosted tenants using the old proxy image.

priya: Confirmed — ~120 hosted orgs use the image; 7 enterprise accounts had custom routing but are on newer images. I'll share the CSV in the ticket.

sam: SLA question — if we take emergency maintenance will that count as allowed maintenance (no SLA credit) or incident (potential credit)? We need to minimize SLA hit for enterprise.

maya: If we push a hotfix with rolling restarts <5% errors and no sustained downtime, we can classify as maintenance. But we should coordinate a canary and keep retry/fallback routes to avoid 502s.

alex: Proposed plan: 1) emergency patch image build (taylor) 2) canary on 2 hosts in prod region-us-east (no customers pinned) 3) monitor errors/latency 30m 4) gradual rollout controlled by traffic routing policy 5) notify affected customers + support playbook. If canary fails -> rollback and escalate incident.

taylor: I can build a patched image in ~90m. Will include layered rebuild + SBOM update. Patch will require container restart only. Dockerfile change is tiny: `npm audit fix && npm prune` and bump dependency to 3.4.2.

oncall-bot: @oncall_eng notified: sam assigned as incident lead for now. Pager duty: sam -> acknowledged?

sam: Ack. I'll own coordination with SRE and Customer Success. We should prepare two communication templates: one for hosted users (high exposure) and one for Dedicated customers (low exposure, targeted).

priya: Customer comm draft in SEC-2046, short + actionable: "We’re deploying an urgent security patch that requires brief rolling restarts. No action required from you. Contact support if you see errors." Add enterprise note for account teams.

maya: Prioritization checklist: public PoC (yes), exploitability (high), number of exposed customers (120), SLA risk (manageable with rolling canary). Recommendation: emergency rollout now in controlled fashion.

alex: Decision: emergency patch. Taylor starts build; canary in us-east, monitor 30m; if green roll to remaining hosts with staged batch size 10%. Sam to prepare comms and incident channel for updates. Priya to flag any enterprise customers to schedule pinning if needed.

taylor: Starting build now. Pushing image to registry -> `registry.redwood-infer.io/patches/payload-parser:20260305-0487` ETA 1h.

security-bot: mitigation note: temporary WAF rule suggested — block suspicious header patterns until rollout completes. Recommend ops enable WAF rule for 24h.

sam: Agree — enabling WAF rule now. If we see false positives we'll tune.

maya: Also add audit logging hook to capture suspicious requests (header content) for later forensics — link logs to SEC-2046.

alex: Good. After finished rollout, follow-up actions: publish CVE note internally, update SBOMs, run dependency sweep, add regression evals, and schedule postmortem if rollout had customer impact.

priya: I'll schedule customer briefing for affected enterprise accounts and update the status page template.

alex: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread and SEC-2046. :thumbsup:
